opportunities.title: Agro-Processing Hub
opportunities.summary: Add value to Ethiopia's agricultural output with export-ready processing on the Addis–Djibouti corridor.
bullets: Comprehensive analysis of high-potential sectors (e.g., agriculture, manufacturing, renewable energy).
Feasibility studies tailored to client projects
body: Ethiopia is Africa's largest coffee producer and a leading exporter of oilseeds, pulses and horticulture — yet most produce still leaves the country unprocessed. This agro-processing hub near Adama targets that value-add gap.
The site sits on the Addis–Djibouti economic corridor with direct rail access to the port, giving processors a competitive logistics edge for export markets in the Middle East and Europe.
Afrimpact supports investors with sector analysis, site due diligence, licensing through the Ethiopian Investment Commission and introductions to cooperative unions for secure raw-material supply.

opportunities.title: Industrial Park Manufacturing
opportunities.summary: Plug-and-play factory space in a flagship eco-industrial park built for export manufacturers.
bullets: Step-by-step assistance with licensing, taxation, and governance compliance.
body: Plug-and-play factory sheds are available in one of East Africa's flagship eco-industrial parks, built for textile, apparel and light-manufacturing exporters.
Tenants benefit from one-stop-shop government services on site, a zero-liquid-discharge treatment plant and preferential market access under multiple trade agreements.
We coordinate every stakeholder — park administration, customs, labour offices and local suppliers — so your operation is compliant and running faster.

opportunities.title: Solar Mini-Grid Portfolio
opportunities.summary: Equity and blended-finance partners sought for a portfolio of licensed rural solar mini-grids.
bullets: Facilitate partnerships with local businesses, suppliers, and government agencies.
body: A portfolio of 12 licensed solar mini-grid sites serving rural trading centres is seeking equity and blended-finance partners.
Kenya's regulatory framework for mini-grids is among the most mature on the continent, with clear tariff approval processes and results-based financing from development partners.
Afrimpact provides independent risk and viability assessment, including demand studies, tariff modelling and ESG screening.

opportunities.title: Fintech Partnership
opportunities.summary: A licensed Kigali payments company seeks a strategic partner for East African expansion.
bullets: Regulatory sandbox access through the Kigali International Financial Centre
body: A licensed digital-payments company in Kigali is looking for a strategic partner to expand merchant payments into the wider East African Community.
Rwanda's regulatory sandbox and investor-friendly financial-centre regime make it an ideal launchpad for fintech products targeting regional markets.
We guide partners through central-bank licensing, data-protection requirements and cross-border compliance.

opportunities.title: Mixed-Use Real Estate
opportunities.summary: Grade-A offices and serviced apartments in Africa's diplomatic capital.
bullets: Located on the new Addis corridor development
body: Addis Ababa hosts the African Union and over 100 diplomatic missions, driving sustained demand for quality office space and serviced residences.
This mixed-use development combines Grade-A offices, retail and serviced apartments along a newly upgraded city corridor.
Afrimpact supports land-lease review, partner vetting and structuring of foreign-currency returns.

opportunities.title: Eco-Lodge Development
opportunities.summary: A community-partnered eco-lodge at one of Ethiopia's most striking crater lakes.
bullets: Growing domestic and international visitor numbers
body: Wonchi crater lake is one of the most striking landscapes in Ethiopia and a fast-growing destination for domestic and international visitors.
The opportunity is a 40-key eco-lodge developed in partnership with the local community association, following low-impact building standards.
We combine investment advisory and travel expertise to validate demand, design the guest experience and secure permits.

opportunities.title: Entoto, Addis Ababa
opportunities.summary: Eucalyptus forests, panoramic city views and historic churches on the hills above the capital.
body: Rising more than 3,000 metres above sea level, the Entoto hills offer cool air, eucalyptus forests and sweeping views over Addis Ababa.
The recently developed Entoto Park adds walking trails, cafés, an adventure park and cultural spaces, making it a perfect half-day escape for business travelers and families alike.
Afrimpact can arrange guided hikes, cultural visits and transport as part of a tailored Addis Ababa itinerary.

opportunities.title: Wonchi, Oromia
opportunities.summary: A volcanic crater lake with hot springs, island monastery and community-run horse treks.
bullets: Boat trip to Cherkos monastery island
body: Wonchi is a collapsed volcanic caldera holding a pristine crater lake, surrounded by farmland, forest and small villages.
Visitors can ride down to the lake with community guides, take a boat to the island monastery of Cherkos and relax at nearby hot springs.
It pairs perfectly with the Wonchi eco-lodge investment opportunity for investors who want to see the destination first-hand.

opportunities.title: Fasiledes, Gonder
opportunities.summary: The UNESCO-listed royal enclosure of Fasil Ghebbi, the 'Camelot of Africa'.
body: Founded in the 17th century by Emperor Fasilides, Gondar was Ethiopia's royal capital for more than two centuries.
The Fasil Ghebbi fortress-city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and Fasilides' Bath hosts one of the most spectacular Timkat (Epiphany) celebrations in the country each January.
We arrange expert heritage guides, domestic flights and accommodation as part of Ethiopia's Historic Route.

opportunities.title: Jegol, Harar
opportunities.summary: The walled city of Harar — colourful alleys, historic mosques and lively markets.
body: Harar Jugol is a UNESCO World Heritage fortified city with 368 alleyways squeezed into one square kilometre.
Its colourful markets, historic mosques and traditional Harari houses make it one of the most atmospheric destinations in the Horn of Africa.
Afrimpact arranges local guides, cultural home visits and connections for travelers extending their trip to Dire Dawa.
highlights: Fly to Dire Dawa then 1 hour by road

opportunities.title: Simien Mountains
opportunities.summary: Dramatic escarpments, gelada monkeys and some of Africa's finest multi-day treks.
body: The Simien Mountains National Park is a UNESCO site of jagged peaks, deep valleys and sheer escarpments.
Trekkers regularly encounter troops of gelada monkeys and may spot the rare walia ibex and Ethiopian wolf.
We organise permits, scouts, mules and lodge or camping logistics for treks of 2 to 10 days.

opportunities.title: Danakil Depression
opportunities.summary: Lava lakes, salt flats and otherworldly colours in one of the hottest places on Earth.
body: The Danakil Depression lies more than 100 metres below sea level and is one of the most geologically active places on the planet.
Expeditions visit the glowing Erta Ale lava lake, the acid-yellow springs of Dallol and the salt flats where Afar caravans still cut salt blocks by hand.
We work only with licensed operators and include security briefings, experienced drivers and full camping support.

opportunities.title: Additional Opportunities
opportunities.summary: Feasibility assessments for combined investment and travel opportunities.
bullets: Feasibility assessments for combined investment and travel opportunities.
body: Many of the best opportunities in Africa sit at the intersection of investment and travel — hospitality, eco-tourism, conference facilities and agri-tourism among them.
Our combined feasibility assessments evaluate market demand, visitor flows, regulatory requirements and financial returns in one integrated study.
Share your idea with us and we will scope an assessment tailored to your timeline and budget.

opportunities.title: Additional Opportunities
opportunities.summary: Risk and viability analysis for sustainable development projects.
bullets: Risk and viability analysis for sustainable development projects.
body: Development finance institutions and impact investors increasingly require rigorous risk and ESG analysis before committing capital.
Afrimpact delivers independent risk and viability assessments covering political, currency, operational and environmental and social risk.
Our reports are structured to support investment committee decisions and lender due diligence.

news.title: Afrimpact Consultancy has been launched officially
news.author: Lucy Hiddleston
news.excerpt: Afrimpact Consultancy officially opens its doors in Addis Ababa, offering integrated investment and travel advisory across Africa.
body: Afrimpact Consultancy has officially launched in Addis Ababa, bringing together investment advisory and travel expertise under one roof.
## A single gateway to Africa

Investors and travelers often face the same challenges when arriving in a new African market: unfamiliar regulations, fragmented information and the need for trusted local partners. Afrimpact was founded to close that gap.
Our team offers market entry strategies, regulatory and compliance guidance, stakeholder engagement, tailored itineraries and visa support — all coordinated by one advisor.
## What comes next

Over the coming months we will publish sector briefings, destination guides and events designed to help clients make confident decisions. Subscribe to our newsletter to be the first to hear about new opportunities.

news.title: Expansion of our consultancy services to southern Africa
news.author: Lucy Hiddleston
news.excerpt: We are extending our advisory coverage to southern African markets, starting with partnerships in Zambia and Botswana.
body: Following strong demand from clients, Afrimpact is extending its advisory services to southern Africa.
## Why southern Africa
The region offers mature regulatory frameworks, growing renewable-energy pipelines and world-class tourism destinations — a natural fit for our combined investment and travel model.
We will begin with partner networks in Zambia and Botswana and add further markets through 2027.

news.title: Africa investment outlook: five sectors to watch in 2027
news.author: Lucy Hiddleston
news.excerpt: Agro-processing, renewable energy, fintech, logistics and tourism top our list of sectors with the strongest fundamentals.
body: Africa continues to offer some of the world's most compelling long-term growth stories. Here are five sectors our team is watching closely.
## 1. Agro-processing
Adding value to raw agricultural output remains one of the largest untapped opportunities on the continent.
## 2. Renewable energy
Mini-grids and utility-scale solar are expanding quickly, supported by blended-finance instruments.
## 3. Fintech
Mobile money adoption continues to create room for payments, lending and insurance innovation.
## 4. Logistics
Trade corridors and the AfCFTA are raising demand for warehousing and cold chain.
## 5. Tourism
Eco-tourism and heritage destinations are attracting new visitors and new capital.

news.title: A practical guide to Ethiopia's e-Visa for business travelers
news.author: Lucy Hiddleston
news.excerpt: Everything you need to know before applying — documents, processing times and common mistakes to avoid.
body: Most visitors to Ethiopia can apply for an e-Visa online before travel. Here is what business travelers should know.
## Documents
Prepare a passport valid for at least six months, a digital passport photo and, for business visas, an invitation letter from a local host company.
## Processing time
Applications are typically processed within a few working days, but we recommend applying at least two weeks before travel.
## How we help

Afrimpact reviews your documents, prepares invitation letters for client visits and tracks your application until approval. Always confirm current requirements with official government sources before travel.

news.title: When to visit: planning your Ethiopia trip around the seasons
news.author: Lucy Hiddleston
news.excerpt: From the green season to festival months, here's how to time your visit for the experiences you want.
body: Ethiopia's highland climate is mild year-round, but the seasons shape what you can see and do.
## October – March
The dry season is ideal for trekking in the Simien Mountains, visiting the Historic Route and exploring the Danakil Depression.
## Festivals
Meskel (late September) and Timkat (January) are spectacular cultural celebrations worth planning around.
## June – September
The rainy season turns the highlands lush and green, with fewer visitors and lower prices.
